verdict.quote: Developer Edition provides a free and easy solution so that you can use Salesforce for testing and development.
verdict.reason: A free Developer Edition org has API access by default, so credentials are self-serve. The commercial-use / ISV clause in the API terms is not one of the rubric's friction triggers. (developer.salesforce.com HTML pages returned 403, so the quote is from Salesforce's official REST API guide PDF.)

mcp.quote: An official, reliable and fully supported connection built and maintained by Pipedrive.
mcp.reason: Pipedrive launched and hosts its own native MCP server (announced June 2026); community servers also exist but the vendor one makes it official.

mcp.quote: Twenty exposes an MCP server so that AI assistants
mcp.reason: Twenty's own docs describe a built-in MCP server configured under Settings > AI > MCP, so it is first-party, not community.

mcp.quote: The server is live at https://mcp.podio.com — just point your AI platform at it and log in with your Podio account.
mcp.reason: Progress (Podio's owner) documents its own hosted MCP server at mcp.podio.com, currently in beta.

verdict.quote: Close doesn't have a free plan, but you can try it free for 14 days with no credit card.
verdict.reason: The only self-serve path is a 14-day trial. The free Dev org requires emailing support and is limited to integration partners. A short time-limited trial is friction under the rubric.

mcp.reason: Close documents and hosts its own MCP server on its developer site.

access.quote: Every plan starts with a 14-day free trial, and no credit card is required.
access.reason: No free plan; API is on Professional/Business, which can be trialled for 14 days without a card (trial-includes-API is confirmed only by third-party integrator docs, so moderate confidence).

mcp.quote: We'll share both at public release.
mcp.reason: Copper's own server is still listed as coming soon behind a waitlist/beta, so it is not yet published; third-party servers (e.g. dazanza/copper-mcp, Cotlet, Activepieces) do exist.

mcp.quote: DealCloud now provides a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server which gives AI agents read access to your DealCloud data.
mcp.reason: DealCloud's release notes announce its own MCP server (Celeste license), so an official server exists.

verdict.quote: You can try out the Zendesk platform with a free, 14-day trial account.
verdict.reason: Non-partner builders only get a 14-day trial (sponsored accounts are reserved for Marketplace partners), which the rubric counts as friction.

verdict.quote: When you sign up, you instantly get access to our Enterprise plan for 14 days.
verdict.reason: The pricing page lists only paid plans and a 14-day trial, with no free plan, so the only free path is a short trial.

mcp.quote: MCP is enabled by default for your Freshdesk instance.
mcp.reason: Freshworks' own support docs describe a built-in Freshdesk MCP server, not a third-party one.
Front documents and hosts its own MCP server on its developer portal.

mcp.quote: The Pylon MCP Server exposes Pylon data to AI tools that support the Model Context Protocol
mcp.reason: Pylon documents and hosts its own MCP server on its docs domain.

mcp.quote: LiveAgent exposes a built-in MCP server (Model Context Protocol)
mcp.reason: The vendor's own support docs describe a built-in, vendor-hosted MCP server.

verdict.quote: Start with a 7-day free trial, no credit card required.
verdict.reason: There is no free plan. The only free path is a 7-day trial, which is a short time-limited trial.

access.quote: Start with a 7-day free trial, no credit card required.
access.reason: A self-serve trial exists, so the agent's paid_plan is wrong. The manual 'self_serve' label maps to the right answer, but its 'free tier' claim is wrong: it is a trial, not a free plan.

mcp.reason: Plain documents and hosts its own MCP server.

mcp.quote: Help Scout MCP gives AI assistants secure, official access to Help Scout data.
mcp.reason: Help Scout runs a vendor-hosted remote MCP server at mcp.helpscout.net.

verdict.quote: The Gorgias trial period lasts 7 days.
verdict.reason: No free plan exists, so the only free path is a short 7-day trial, which the rubric counts as friction.

access.quote: No, you don't need to enter payment info to start the Gorgias trial.
access.reason: The API is on all helpdesk plans, and a no-card 7-day trial with all features gives credentials, so this is self_serve_trial, not paid_plan.

mcp.quote: The Gorgias MCP provides a first-party bridge
mcp.reason: Gorgias publishes its own MCP server at mcp.gorgias.com.

mcp.quote: StackOne's Gladly MCP server ships with 65 pre-built actions
mcp.reason: Gladly publishes no MCP server, but third parties (StackOne, Truto, usefulapi) offer Gladly MCP servers, so community rather than none.

access.quote: Yes. Aircall offers free access to test the platform before committing.
access.reason: There is a free self-serve trial and 'All plans include API access', so the access is not paid-only. The trial length, and whether the API works during the trial, are not stated, so confidence is moderate.

mcp.quote: an AI assistant, like Claude or ChatGPT, read-only access to your company's calls
mcp.reason: Aircall's help center documents its own beta, read-only MCP at mcp.aircall.io/mcp, which returns 401 without auth. The developer FAQ saying there is no MCP is stale.

verdict.quote: Visit your app's Product tab in the Developer Portal to apply for the Advertising API product.
verdict.reason: Access is a self-serve application from the developer portal with a Development tier to build and test, which is vendor approval (friction), not a partnership or sales conversation.

access.quote: LinkedIn reserves the right to review applications and select partners at its discretion
access.reason: Developer apps are self-serve but the Advertising API product is granted by LinkedIn review with Development/Standard tiering, matching the app_review definition.

access.quote: Start with a FREE 14-day trial on any plan below!
access.reason: There is no free plan, but a 14-day trial on any plan is self-serve, so this is self_serve_trial rather than paid_plan.

mcp.quote: Our MCP specifically allows you to interact with the Transactional Messaging API
mcp.reason: Mailchimp's own developer site documents a vendor-hosted MCP at mandrillapp.com/mcp (Transactional only, not the Marketing API), which still counts as official.

verdict.quote: Create a new integration on Admin.
verdict.reason: The free Magento Open Source build exposes the same web API, so a developer can self-host and create an integration for credentials. Self-hosting and per-merchant integrations are not rubric friction.

access.quote: Registering an OAuth client, and having it reviewed and approved, only allows OAuth connections with Squarespace.
access.reason: The multi-user OAuth path a toolkit needs is gated by Squarespace review (no paid plan stated for it), while paid Commerce Advanced applies only to single-site API keys; borderline, since neither path is fully self-serve free.

verdict.quote: Email us to get a free plan upgrade for your test store.
verdict.reason: The builder must either pay or email Ecwid for an upgrade before the API works, which is friction.

access.quote: Only stores on paid plans can access API.
access.reason: The free store excludes the API, and a free plan that excludes the API is not self_serve_free under the rubric.

verdict.quote: Amazon reviews your application and sends you an email to the email address associated with your developer profile.
verdict.reason: Self-serve registration followed by Amazon review is app-review friction, not a sales or partnership conversation.

access.quote: Amazon reviews your application and sends you an email to the email address associated with your developer profile.
access.reason: The rubric names Amazon SP-API as an app_review example: the developer profile is self-serve and Amazon then reviews it and the requested roles.

access.quote: The 14-day free trial gives you 100K API credits across all six API endpoints
access.reason: The API is usable in a no-card 14-day trial before any payment is needed, so the access is not paid-only.

verdict.quote: The developer platform is available across all Clay plans, including free, trial, and Legacy plans.
verdict.reason: A documented public API with self-serve keys on the free plan means a builder can start now; its narrow scope is not outreach.

access.quote: The developer platform is available across all Clay plans, including free, trial, and Legacy plans.
access.reason: API keys are created via the CLI on any plan including free; there is a public API, contradicting the manual's 'no general public API'.

verdict.quote: On the Free tier, you get up to five Basic hosts with 1-day metric retention, at no cost.
verdict.reason: A permanent free tier, plus the trial, gives API and app keys self-serve, and partner-registered OAuth is not a rubric friction item.

mcp.reason: Harvest runs a live MCP endpoint at api.harvestapp.com/mcp that uses Harvest's own OAuth server, and its help center has a 'Harvest MCP' article (support.getharvest.com/hc/en-us/articles/46293697226381; Cloudflare blocked a direct fetch, seen only through search).

verdict.quote: These models only apply to Production traffic; usage of Sandbox is always free.
verdict.reason: A free, fully featured Sandbox gives working keys immediately, plus a free Trial plan with real data for US/CA teams. Production approval does not block building.

access.quote: Using a Trial plan, you can use Plaid with real production data for free.
access.reason: The free dev sandbox counts as self_serve_free under the rubric. Meaningful real-data use is also free via the Trial plan without review, so it is not app_review.

gopaygent.com and its /developers/docs and /pricing pages returned only a title on fetch, and no vendor page confirmed either a free plan with API keys or a reseller/NMI merchant-account model; product identity itself is ambiguous.

verdict.reason: Free API keys from the dashboard are enough to build and test the 3-endpoint API (medium confidence, because the /developers page cites a $99 Developer plan).

access.reason: The vendor docs state a free API-key tier issued from the dashboard, which conflicts with the agent's paid_plan.

verdict.quote: Please contact our developer support team to be issued a client ID and client secret for partner authentication.
verdict.reason: Per-account tokens are self-serve on the free Essentials plan, but multi-user OAuth needs Brex to approve the partner and issue credentials by hand: friction, not outreach for basic access.

access.reason: The self-serve $0/user Essentials tier lists 'Brex API access', and an admin of your own account can create a token, so access is not partner-gated.

mcp.quote: The server is hosted at https://api.brex.com/mcp and supports any MCP-compatible client.
mcp.reason: Brex documents and hosts its own MCP server.

verdict.quote: After Ramp approves your production access application, onboard production customers through OAuth.
verdict.reason: A sandbox is self-serve via a form (ready in about a minute), but multi-customer use needs Ramp's approval. That is app review, not outreach.

access.quote: Your sandbox should be ready in about one minute.
access.reason: Sandbox credentials are self-serve, and production for other businesses requires an approval application. That matches app_review, not partner_gated.

verdict.quote: During the preview, the API is available for personal Google Accounts.
verdict.reason: The Gemini Notebook API is an open public preview usable with a personal Google account and no allowlist or licence; Workspace exclusion is not a builder blocker.

access.quote: The Gemini Notebook API is free to use during the Public Preview period,
access.reason: Free during public preview with a Free tier listed; the manual cited the older enterprise-licensed NotebookLM Enterprise API instead.

verdict.reason: The docs never state whether the Free or Pro plans get API keys, so ready vs ready_with_friction cannot be settled.

access.reason: API key setup is documented for Teams/org service users, but no page says whether Free accounts get API access (paid_plan likely but unconfirmed).
